source: Invest Like the Best — Why the markets are pricing AI wrong: July 2026 AI/semis selloff, private inference cloud, old-GPU repricing, ~$700B Blackwell/Rubin credit gap
summary: July 2026 AI/semis selloff was a sentiment-driven overreaction ('2022 in a month') with no negative quantitative fundamentals to justify it
summary_extended: Baker argues that the July 2026 AI/semiconductor selloff — in which leading AI names fell 40-60% from their highs in a straight line — was a pure sentiment-driven overreaction with no fundamental justification, analogizing it to 'what 2022 felt like but compressed into a single month.' He pressure-tested every quantitative assumption during a dedicated Silicon Valley trip and found zero negative data points: GPU availability, GPU retail pricing, DRAM spot prices, and token/inference growth were all accelerating, not decelerating. The implication is that the selloff created a significant buying opportunity in AI infrastructure and semiconductor names, as the market mispriced a sentiment shock as a fundamental deterioration. Baker frames this as his highest-conviction thesis for the episode, with the recovery thesis predicated on the divergence between collapsing equity prices and uniformly positive real-time supply-chain and demand metrics.
